notes: §1985:VI.6.11.4 GR6 defines the remainder as the dividend less the product of the quotient and the divisor, the quotient for an edited or ROUNDED identifier-3 being an intermediate field 'truncated rather than rounded' with 'the same presence or absence of a sign as the quotient (identifier-3)'. ArithmeticEmitter.EmitDivideRemainder forms the truncated subsidiary quotient at identifier-3's scale (SubsidiaryShapeOf, NativeSubsidiaryQuotient, CarriedSubsidiaryQuotient, FixedPointSubsidiary), and UnsignedSubsidiary, the edition arm landed by kb/Work PB5182, takes its absolute value when the dialect is below 2002 and identifier-3 is fixed-point with no sign; the prior read's PARTIAL (a signed subsidiary for an unsigned identifier-3) is closed. Probed at --std 85 against 2002: (d) DIVIDE -11 BY 3 GIVING PIC 9 REMAINDER gives 3 and -20.00 (2002: -2.00), ROUNDED gives 4 and -20.00, a signed PIC S9 gives -3 and -2.00 at both, 11 BY -3 gives 3 and +20.00, PIC 9V9 gives 3.6 and -21.80, edited ZZ9.9 gives 3.6 and -21.80 (ROUNDED 3.7 and -21.80), a signed edited -ZZ9.9 and a CR item give -0.20, an unsigned COMP and COMP-3 quotient give 333 and -2000, an unsigned remainder takes 20.00; (f) 18 digits: -999999999999999999 BY 1 into PIC 9(18) keeps the 85 formula; a zero divisor and a quotient size error leave both receivers unchanged under ON SIZE ERROR; a subscripted quotient TQE (I) gives 3 and -20.00. The witness divides 11 by 3 GIVING PIC 9 ROUNDED (4, remainder 2); pb5182-unsigned-quotient-remainder-1985 covers the sign arm. next.reason: 1985: "the same presence or absence of a sign as the quotient (identifier-3)"; 2023: "a subsidiary quotient is developed that is signed and derived from the quotient by truncation of digits". Both define remainder as dividend minus truncated quotient times divisor, but 2023 always uses a signed subsidiary quotient. 1985 follows identifier-3's sign, so unsigned quotients differ.
